documents.title: Pokémon Changes
documents.summary: Per-Pokémon type, base stat, ability, held item, evolution and learnset changes.

generalNotes.title: General Changes
lines: - The Fairy-type has been added to the game, replacing the almost unused ???-type.
- All Pokémon have had their base stats updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.
- All Pokémon have had their types updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.
- All Pokémon have had their wild held item updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon (with some exceptions).
- All Pokémon now have an egg cycle of 0, i.e. they will hatch extremely quickly.
- Wingull, Pelipper and Torkoal have gained their new abilities from Gen VII.
- Pokémon that evolved with items which could no longer learn moves on level up now have full level-up sets.
This was changed since I personally never liked this mechanic, as it meant you might have to wait a long time
with an underpowered Pokémon just to get the move you want. This is dissimilar to the Pokémon which previously
evolved with held items during a trade, which can use their items now with no strings attached.
I feel consistency with these Pokémon is the best option, and it makes them easier to train.

generalNotes.title: Effort Value Removal
lines: Effort Values are completely gone. Just entirely absent.
This was done for a variety of reasons- the difficulty of this hack is intended to be based on tactical decisions,
teambuilding and things like that- not on being a munchkin and trying to create the ultimate life-form.
As well, opposing trainers can't use EVs anyway, so it's more balanced this way. You no longer have to worry about
accidentally EV training your Jolteon with Attack and HP EVs, and such. IVs and natures are comparatively less
impactful, and with Synchronize desirable natures can still be acquired if you really want them.
With non-optimal IVs/Natures, your Pokémon have a marginal disadvantage, but the AI, even at max level, isn't the smartest
anyway, so it can be thought of as a sort of handicap to make the trainers more dangerous.

generalNotes.title: Held Item Exceptions
lines: - Pokémon who may hold an item in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon that doesn't exist in Platinum will not hold anything.
- Corsola has a 5% chance to hold a Hard Stone.
- Pelipper has a 5% chance to hold a Lucky Egg.
- Sinnohan Absol has a 5% chance to hold a Life Orb.
- Spiritomb has a 100% chance to hold a Smoke Ball.

generalNotes.title: Other Changes
lines: - Some Pokémon have ability slots flipped (e.g. Scizor). This is because enemy Trainers always use the first ability.
- The rate for Shiny Pokémon is now 1/512, instead of 1/8192.
- Many of the shiny Pokémon I thought looked hideous have had entirely new palettes added.
Some I've changed just because I wanted to, but a large majority of shinies are unchanged. Either because I doubt most
people care about them, or because I already like them enough.
All starters except Venusaur, Charizard and Meganium have new shinies, though!
Also- Onix and Steelix are based on the Crystal Onix from the anime!

generalNotes.title: Ability changes
lines: Several abilities have been renamed so that they can apply to more Pokémon. The purpose of this is to increase ability variety,
by adding 'new' clone abilities(like Huge Power/Pure Power) with a more general concept, so more Pokémon can benefit.
Generation 4 has a lack of abilities I would like to implement if it was possible, so this is a nice compromise.
All of these abilities do exactly the same thing- the rename is only meant to make them fit on more Pokémon.
Clear Body has been renamed to Strong Body.
New description: "Its toughness prevents stat reduction."
New users: Hitmonchan, Pinsir, Heracross, Skarmory, Whiscash, Armaldo, Piplup/Prinplup/Empoleon, Snover
Download has been renamed to Instinct.
New description: "Boosts an offense based on foe's weakness."
New users: Nidoking, Voltorb/Electrode, Sceptile, Kecleon, Deoxys, Mothim, Lucario, Toxicroak, Sinnohan Furret
Compound Eyes has been renamed to Deadeye.
New description: "Amazing senses boost its accuracy."
New users: Pidgeot, Seel, Dewgong, Starmie, Persian, Kecleon, Sinnohan Scyther, Sinnohan Flygon
Rock Head has been renamed to Determined.
New description: "Its sheer determination prevents recoil damage."
New users: Charizard, Tauros, Flareon, Ursaring, Blaziken
Own Tempo has been renamed to Simple Mind.
New description: "Its clear thoughts prevent confusion."
New users: Primeape
Sturdy has been entirely removed from the game, as one-hit KO moves no longer exist.
Lightning Rod and Storm Drain have also been entirely removed from the game. This is because in Gen 4, they lack their
Electric/Water immunity attributes, as well as the Special Attack boost, and ONLY redirect these moves during double battles,
making them ludicrously terrible. Most instances have been replaced with Volt Absorb/Motor Drive and Water Absorb.

generalNotes.title: Custom Changes
lines: From the bases as listed above, further changes to any Pokémon are listed below. These can include changes to base stats, abilities, types etcetera.
Some Pokémon have had a Hidden Ability from a later generation added as a regular ability (e.g. Torkoal).
TM compatibilty with any of the new TMs (Bug Buzz, Hurricane) is also listed here.
Any move previously unavailable to a Pokémon is listed with a (!!) besides it.
If a move was added to a Pokémon because of Pokémon Legends: Arceus, it will be listed with a (PLA) besides it.

Level up moves have also been changed for every single Pokémon. These should include all moves they learn in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon that are available in Altered Platinum, as well as additional moves from move tutors, egg moves or entirely new techniques.
Each Pokémon is listed under its own section header below.

documents.title: Sinnohan Forms
documents.summary: The 65 Sinnohan regional forms: types, abilities, stats, evolutions and learnsets.

generalNotes.title: General Notes
lines: - Sinnohan Forms are new regional variants with the same general concept as Alolan Forms- new type, abilities, stats and moves.
Unlike Alolan Forms, though, they totally replace the originals, due to engine limitations.
They also cannot breed.
There are a total of 30 Sinnohan Forms- three times the number of Alolan Forms, and 10 per region prior to Sinnoh.
None of these have been rushed, and were completed gradually over a long period of time as new ideas came in.
Though some might be a little overpowered, they were designed to be mostly balanced(compared to the new standard of power).
It's singleplayer anyway, so it's not like it matters too much!
A large blank space has been added below in case you decide to avoid spoilers.

documents.title: Type Changes
documents.summary: The Ice type-chart rework and the 69 Pokémon type changes with justifications.

generalNotes.title: General Changes
lines: Fairy-type is now in the game, replacing what was previously the ??? type.
All Pokémon that are Fairy-type in Gen VI onwards are also Fairy-type in Altered Platinum.
Rotom's five alternate forms take the secondary type that they have in the Gen V games and onward (they are not Ghost-type like the normal Platinum).
As in Generation VI games and onward, Steel takes 1x damage from Dark and Ghost attacks.
Some fossil Pokemon are no longer Rock-type. If I think the type benefitted them, it remained.

generalNotes.title: Ice Type Changes
lines: - Ice is the only type which has had its relations changed from vanilla- this is because I feel Ice is a grossly underpowered type.
- The changes made were chosen both for thematic and gameplay reasons. Ice's resistances do not nerf already-underpowered offensive types.
- With these changes, Ice is still weak to the common Fire and Fighting, plus Steel, but its key resistances to popular attacking types give Ice a real
chance to take on a defensive role. Ground, Water and Dragon are very common offensive types without a lot of competition- and they are all,
at least on offense, perhaps better than they deserve to be. With Ice resisting these, but still being weak to a couple of popular types as before,
it is balanced out, and allows for more interesting things to be done with the type as a whole.
- Keeping type chart changes limited to Ice also makes it easier to remember.

generalNotes.title: General Changes
lines: The numbers of all moves (power, accuracy, PP, effect chance, priority) are updated to match Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.
Curse is now a Ghost-type move as in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.
Charm, Moonlight and Sweet Kiss are now Fairy-type as in Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.

generalNotes.title: General Changes
lines: - Trainer rosters in every area has been modified. They are all listed below with species and levels.
- Important trainers have their entire roster listed including species, levels, items, and moves.
- Gym Leaders have been totally reworked- they have a new set of themes based on a central mechanic and concept.
- Some postgame Trainers have a * next to their name. This signals that you need to beat them to advance into Stark Mountain.
- Some trainers have a (!) next to their name. This means that they have further rosters via the Vs. Seeker.
- Some trainers have a (3) or other number next to their name. This means they should start using these teams once you have that number of badges.
- Instead of a number, you may see a (C) for Champion or (S) for Stark Mountain, which means after completing these they'll gain those teams.
- Please note that the number of badges may not always be correct. Feel free to report any incorrect information!
- Sinnohan Forms are marked by an (S) after the Pokémon's name. Note that they replace the originals, however, so this is only for convenience.

documents.summary: Wild encounters by area, method and time of day.

generalNotes.title: General Changes
lines: The Wild Pokémon in each area have been modified.
The levels listed for an area are the minimum and maximum levels that you may encounter in that area.
Please note that many Pokémon can only be encountered at one specific level. Only some have the range.
Fishing rod encounters have levels based on area.
The different rods have been replaced by Lures, new items obtained and used in the same way, which do not change level, but instead change what Pokémon you encounter.
The Worm Lure and Berry Lure are obtainable from the same places as the Old Rod and Good Rod, respectively. The Fish Lure is obtainable in Snowpoint City.
While the lures are meant to attract certain kinds of Pokémon, small, closed off bodies of water have only a limited range of different species.
Oceans, rivers, and cave lakes connected to underground rivers have the widest variety. Lakes are average, and isolated ponds are the least varied.
Honey trees now respond with an encounter straight away after applying Honey.
Please note that the shiny rate for Pokémon is 1/512.

Some Pokémon are only found when using the Poké Radar (these are listed as Poké Radar). These Pokémon may show up when you enter the patches with the yellow sparkles (NOT the shiny sparkles, that's something else!)
Sinnohan Forms are marked by an (S) after the Pokémon's name. Note that they replace the originals, however, so this is only for convenience.
